target: Let E carry its original real norm and admit algebraic linear coordinates in R^d. Let f:E→[-infinity,+infinity] be proper and closed, and lambda>0. Suppose f satisfies lambda-strong convexity on its effective domain and the global subdifferential in the given coordinates is nonempty at some point. Then there is exactly one p in the effective domain such that f(p)<=f(q) for every q in E. The source ambient R^d is represented by a real normed space with an algebraic linear equivalence to Euclidean coordinates. The original norm is used in every strong-convexity and growth inequality; the coordinate map need not preserve that norm. Properness excludes bottom globally and supplies a finite value. Closedness means closed real sublevel cuts. Strong interpolation is quantified on all finite-domain pairs with strictly interior weights. The one actual global coordinate subgradient witness is retained. Convexity of the domain and finite-dimensional proper-space compactness are derived. No minimizer, coercivity, compact domain or support at all points is an input.

cross_route_blind_spot_audit.canonical_route: Choose an actual supported point y and covector g. Properness makes y finite. The source growth theorem and the continuous-dual norm of v↦<g,e(v)> bound the sublevel S={x:f(x)<=f(y)} inside the original-norm closed ball of radius 2||L||/lambda about y. Closedness and derived finite-dimensionality make S compact. Apply the actual Appendix A.3 producer to obtain p minimizing f on S, then compare every point outside S against f(y) to obtain global minimality. Finally the actual minimum-growth theorem and positive curvature force uniqueness.
